scope: six distinct publications, author-reported evidence and independence, no scientific reproduction

studies.study: Lind et al 2015 experimental Pseudomonas alternative phenotype routes
studies.unit: 200 independent founder microcosms after engineered 3-route knockout; 91 endpoint morphologies
studies.findings: 10 alternate single-step paths and 3 multi-step, 109 negative populations at 6-day window
studies.independence: Different experimental cohort from Rainey group Beaumont 2009 and Gallie 2015, but same model species and shared cellular machinery
studies.caveat: exogenous deletion and selection for old phenotype; not self-built ecological constraint or new organism

studies.study: Taylor et al 2016 yeast cross genotype-phenotype epistasis
studies.unit: 106 independently initiated parent crosses, >100000 progeny tested, 17 independently selected rough segregants
studies.findings: 8 novel mutation interactions, 9 standing variant recombinations; common pathway components
studies.independence: Separate yeast genetic-cross study, distinct laboratory and species from the Pseudomonas route studies; not origin of a new species
studies.caveat: morphology proxy, unknown ecological utility, shared parent lines

studies.study: Johnson and Desai 2022 mutational neighborhood changes
studies.unit: 12 long-term evolved populations from earlier historical experiment, 144 nested sampled clones, 91 introduced gene disruption perturbations
studies.findings: mean mutational effects decreased in one evolving environment, not detectably in the second
studies.independence: reuses older original yeast evolution population data with new mutation-effect assays; not new independent long-term evolution origins
studies.caveat: fitness robustness not same as new function discovery or within-life learning

studies.study: Routh et al 2025 stable-environment yeast evolution then stress
studies.unit: three ancestor-related evolved lines after ~1000 generations
studies.findings: fitness in novel stress often reduced, adaptation mainly from de novo mutations not prior cryptic pool
studies.independence: separate research cohort from Taylor and Johnson yeast experiments
studies.caveat: source-level abstract/selected-method reading only; full raw stress replicates not audited

studies.study: Sakuma et al 2026 enzyme single-molecule functional substates
studies.unit: one wild-type and 18 previously evolved selected variants; new single-molecule tests, not 18 evolutionary cohorts
studies.findings: native and alternate catalytic-state distributions shift over previously selected trajectory
studies.independence: References 45-46 share the earlier PTE trajectory studies with Kaltenbach 2016 references 29 and 33: Tokuriki 2012 and Kaltenbach 2015. New measurement study, not independent origin; exact per-variant overlap not audited.
studies.caveat: metal/cofactor heterogeneity alters peaks; simulation model does not prove selection of ecological benefit

studies.study: Kaltenbach et al 2016 enzyme promiscuity and tradeoff
studies.unit: Mutation-effect assays for one laboratory-evolved PTE/AE transition and one characterized natural AtzA/TriA transition
studies.findings: native function not always more robust to mutation than promiscuous one, contradicts simplistic universal explanation
studies.independence: PTE source trajectories overlap Sakuma 2026 via Tokuriki 2012 and Kaltenbach 2015; the other functional transition is natural rather than a second laboratory evolution.
studies.caveat: selection bias, highly specific prepared molecular assays, not ecological-reproductive proof

negative_cases: Lind: 109/200 populations no target morphology during 6-day test, despite route deletion
Taylor: only 17 positive unusual phenotype isolates from >100000 progeny; cryptic combinations not independently selected ecological capabilities
Johnson: one of two experimental conditions did not show change in mean disruptive-mutation effects
Routh: stable selection often reduced new-stress adaptation, cryptic variants not significant route
Sakuma: metal/cofactor preparation can produce substate heterogeneity; evolved enzymes not new organisms
